Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the run chase. The umpires are out in the middle. Indian players are huddled in the middle, before they take their respective field positions. For now, Shubman Gill is off the field, and Shreyas Iyer will take on the duties of the captain. It is going to be a tough task for Afghanistan. Ibrahim Zadran and Rahmanullah Gurbaz open up for Afghanistan. Arshdeep Singh to start with the new ball. Let's go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

A late Afghan fightback - The scoring rate slowed down significantly after the set batters fell, triggering a late lower-order collapse, but the damage was already done. Left-arm spinner Nangeyalia Kharote was the pick of the bowlers under pressure, picking up 4 wickets, while Rashid Khan bagged three. AM Ghazanfar and Mohammad Saleem also chipped in with a wicket apiece. It is the eighth time India have crossed 400 in ODIs, leaving Afghanistan with a monumental mountain to climb. Can Afghanistan come up with something special? Or will India continue to dominate with the ball as well? We shall find out soon. Chase is coming up shortly...

A record-breaking masterclass - What followed was absolute carnage. Gill was aggressive from the get-go, while Kishan played second fiddle early on before exploding into life. The duo put on a massive 224-run stand partnership in 141 balls to get the game totally under control. Both batters targeted the boundaries at will, leaving the fielding side completely clueless and searching for answers. Kishan departed after a stellar 125, but Gill kept motoring along. Gill fell in the 43rd over, but India were already past the 350-run mark by then.

India finish with 402! The hosts have put on a sensational batting display to cross the 400-run mark. While Yashasvi Jaiswal fell early, skipper Rohit Sharma gave the innings quick momentum with a brisk 48 before walking back in the 14th over. The Afghan bowlers found some early joy, but it proved to be a fleeting moment of relief. His dismissal brought Shubman Gill and Ishan Kishan together, and that is when the real fireworks began for the Men in Blue.

Afghanistan (Playing XI) - Rahmanullah Gurbaz (WK), Ibrahim Zadran, Sediqullah Atal, Rahmat Shah, Hashmatullah Shahidi (C), Darwish Rasooli (On debut) (In for Mohammad Nabi), Rashid Khan, Nangeyalia Kharote (In for Azmatullah Omarzai), AM Ghazanfar, Mohammad Saleem and Bilal Sami (In for Ziaur Rahman).

India (Playing XI) - Yashasvi Jaiswal (In for Nitish Kumar Reddy), Rohit Sharma, Shubman Gill (C), Ishan Kishan (WK), Shreyas Iyer, KL Rahul, Washington Sundar, Kuldeep Yadav (In for Harsh Dubey), Gurnoor Brar, Arshdeep Singh and Prince Yadav (On debut) (In for Prasidh Krishna).

The skipper of India - Shubman Gill says that they would have bowled first as well because of the team combination of going with 5 bowlers in this match. Shares that the focus is on putting themselves in different situations and gaining experience, whether that means chasing a target or defending one. Shubman informs that they have made three changes. Adds that Prince Yadav makes his debut, Nitish Kumar Reddy was unavailable for selection due to a quad issue, while Kuldeep Yadav and Yashasvi Jaiswal come into the side.

The captain of Afghanistan - Hashmatullah Shahidi says that the wicket looks fresh, and it could spin a bit in the first half, so they want to bowl first. Mentions that in the last game they played well, but they didn't have enough partnerships, so hopefully the boys learn from it and come good in this game. Informs that Mohammad Nabi misses out due to illness, while Azmatullah Omarzai got injured during the practice session. A series on the line - The Bharat Ratna Shri Atal Bihari Vajpayee Ekana Cricket Stadium in Lucknow carries complicated memories for Afghanistan. Six years ago, this city doubled as their 'home' away from home, a hopeful experiment that ended in a 0-3 ODI whitewash against the West Indies. They return not as guests seeking comfort, but as a team chasing survival. After a seven-wicket defeat in Dharamsala, the visitors find themselves 1-0 down in the three-match series with no room for error. India, by contrast, are settled. Their captain is in ominous form, their debutants have announced themselves, and their bowling attack looks increasingly settled with an eye on the 2027 World Cup. Leading from the front - India's captaincy transition has been seamless. Shubman Gill has not only taken over the leadership reins from Rohit Sharma across formats but has also elevated his batting to another level. His unbeaten 84 in the series opener was a masterclass in chase management, compact, calculated, and entirely in control. With vice-captain Shreyas Iyer expected to play a pivotal role at No. 4, and Ishan Kishan's form, India's top order has the firepower to post or chase down any total. Debutants shine - The biggest takeaways from the first ODI, however, were the debutants. Gurnoor Brar and Harsh Dubey walked onto the international stage and delivered immediately. Brar, the left-arm pacer, picked up 3 for 27, using his height and angle to trouble Afghanistan's batters. Dubey, the all-rounder, complemented him with 3 for 47, showcasing control and variety. Their performances solved two problems at once, India's search for left-arm seam variety and a spin-bowling all-rounder who can bat in the lower order. New combinations settling in - In the absence of rested bowlers like Jasprit Bumrah and Mohammed Siraj, the pace attack has been led ably by Arshdeep Singh and Prasidh Krishna. Washington Sundar's role remains a question mark, as he was given just one over in the last game. Searching for rhythm - India's batting lineup looks deep and explosive, with KL Rahul's stability and finishing ability providing the perfect cushion in the middle order. The one concern, however, remains Rohit Sharma's form. The veteran opener, who continues to have his sights set on the 2027 ODI World Cup, has managed just one half-century in his last five ODI innings. With two games against Afghanistan still to come, he has a valuable opportunity to rediscover his rhythm and remind everyone why he remains one of the most dangerous batters in the format. A lone century - For Afghanistan, the first ODI was a tale of two halves. Rahmanullah Gurbaz played an innings of rare brilliance, 102 off 51 balls, with eight fours and eight sixes, an exhibition of clean, fearless hitting. His century was the only reason Afghanistan reached 194; without it, the total would have been far lower and the contest even more one-sided. Gurbaz remains the most dangerous batter in the side, capable of taking the game away from any bowling attack in the first ten overs. The support cast need to deliver - Alongside the reliable Hashmatullah Shahidi, Ibrahim Zadran is another key batter to watch. In his last six matches, he has scored 413 runs at an impressive average of 68.84, making him Afghanistan's one of the most reliable ODI batter. Sediqullah Atal has also impressed recently, showing good potential, and has emerged as a dependable middle-order option. The familiarity with Lucknow's conditions, however, could work in Afghanistan's favour. They have played here before, and the hot and humid weather is something their players are accustomed to. Spin still threatens - On the bowling front, Rashid Khan remains Afghanistan's primary threat. In his last eight ODI matches, he has taken 16 wickets, numbers that underline his ability to control the middle overs and break partnerships. His battle with Gill and Iyer will be one of the defining match-ups of the series. Mohammad Nabi brings experience and control, while Azmatullah Omarzai has emerged as a genuine all-round option, capable of contributing with both bat and ball. Pitch aids all - The Ekana Stadium in Lucknow has traditionally offered a balanced surface, true bounce early, some assistance for seamers with the new ball, and enough grip for spinners as the innings progresses. Dew could be a factor in the evening, making it harder for spinners to grip the ball, a significant consideration for Afghanistan, whose attack revolves around their slow bowlers. The weather is expected to be hot and humid, particularly in the first half of the game, which could test the fitness and concentration of both sides. India's unbeaten run - The head-to-head between these two sides is remarkably one-sided. India have never lost to Afghanistan in any format across 16 international matches. In ODIs specifically, India have won four of the five meetings, with one tied encounter from the 2018 Asia Cup serving as the only time Afghanistan avoided defeat. But those numbers, as dominant as they are, belong to a different era. This is the first bilateral series, and Afghanistan are a far more accomplished side than the one that made its World Cup debut in 2019. Form (Last 5 completed ODIs, recent first) - IND - WLLWW | AFG - LWWWW. Final thoughts - The first ODI showed exactly why this series should not be taken lightly. India may have secured the early advantage, but Afghanistan once again demonstrated that they have the talent and belief to challenge the world's best on any given day. For the hosts, it is a chance to build momentum and wrap up the series with a game to spare. For Afghanistan, it is an opportunity to respond, level the contest and prove that their recent rise is built on substance rather than reputation. With plenty of quality on both sides and no shortage of motivation, another intriguing battle awaits.
